facts.fact_text: The opposition group Ictimai Palata was planning a demonstration to be held on 19 June 2011 in Baku.
Despite the Baku City Executive Authority's refusal, the organisers decided to hold the demonstration in one of the central areas of Baku, namely near the Puppet Theatre on Seaside Boulevard.
According to the applicant, the demonstration was intended to be peaceful.
According to the applicant, the demonstration was conducted in a peaceful manner.
The applicant attended the demonstration near the Puppet Theatre on Seaside Boulevard on 19 June 2011.
The Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA) refused to authorise the holding of the demonstration at the place indicated by the organisers (the square in front of the Narimanov Cinema in Baku).
Shortly after the demonstration had started, the police started to disperse it.
The applicant was arrested at around 6.10 p.m. on 19 June 2011 during the dispersal operation.

Article 49 of the 1995 Constitution of Azerbaijan provides that everyone has the right, having notified respective governmental bodies in advance, to assemble with other people peacefully and without arms, to organise meetings, demonstrations, protests and marches, and to stage pickets.

Under Article 5 of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998, advance written notification is required in order to agree upon the place and time of an assembly and upon the route of a march, with the purpose of enabling the relevant local executive authority to take necessary measures.
Under Article 5 of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998, the notification must be done in writing five days before the demonstration.

Article 8 §§ IV and V of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provides the relevant local executive authority with broad powers to issue relevant orders so as to prohibit a public assembly.
Article 8 § VI of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provides the relevant local executive authority with broad powers to issue relevant orders so as to stop a public assembly.

Article 9 §§ II and VII of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provides the relevant local executive authority with broad powers to restrict or change the place, route and/or time of a public assembly.
Article 9 § VI of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provides the relevant local executive authority with broad powers to designate specific areas for public assemblies.

At the material time, Article 14 § I(2) of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that police authorities have the power, when necessary, to stop an assembly which has not been notified to the authorities beforehand, save for spontaneous assemblies.

At the material time, Article 14 § I(4) of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that police authorities have the power to apprehend and remove from the place where an event is being held persons who came carrying weapons, rocks, pieces of wood and glass, clubs that may pose a threat to people's life and safety or damage property, as well as explosives, flammables, or radioactive materials.

At the material time, Article 14 § II(2) of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that police authorities have the power to order the organisers and participants of an assembly to use all available opportunities to stop the assembly and to disperse, with regard to the execution of orders specified under Article 8 §§ V and VI of that Law.

At the material time, Article 14 § II(3) of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that police authorities have the power to warn organisers and participants that physical force or exceptional measures will be used against them if the order to stop the assembly and to disperse is not complied with.

At the material time, Article 14 § II(4) of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that police authorities have the power to use physical force or exceptional measures in order to stop an assembly and disperse participants, in accordance with the legislation of the Republic of Azerbaijan.

At the material time, Article 14 § II(5) of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that police authorities have the power to apprehend persons not complying with the order to stop an assembly and disperse.

At the material time, Article 14 § VI of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that the use of physical force or exceptional measures by police officers in all circumstances must be proportionate to an existing threat.

At the material time, Article 298 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO) of 2000 provided that any breach of the rules, set forth under the legislation, on the organisation and holding of assemblies, demonstrations, protests, marches and pickets shall be punishable by a reprimand or a fine of seven to thirteen manats (AZN).

At the material time, Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO) of 2000 provided that deliberate failure by an individual to comply with the lawful order of a police officer or military serviceman carrying out their duties to protect public order shall be punishable by a fine of twenty to twenty-five manats (AZN) or, if that sanction is inadequate in the circumstances of the case and taking into account the character of the offender, by administrative detention for a term of up to fifteen days.

At the material time, Article 376.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO) of 2000 provided that if it is impossible for the lawyer chosen by the person against whom administrative-offence proceedings are being carried out to attend, a judge shall appoint a lawyer for that person, in accordance with the legislation of the Republic of Azerbaijan.

At the material time, Article 376.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO) of 2000 provided that if a person subjected to an administrative arrest has no possibility to hire a lawyer due to his or her financial situation, his or her legal assistance shall be funded by the State, and in this case a lawyer may not refuse to carry out his or her duties.

At the material time, Article 396.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO) of 2000 provided that an authorised official may use measures to secure administrative-offence proceedings, including administrative arrest (Article 396.1.2), in order to prevent administrative offences, to establish the identity of a person, to draw up an administrative-offence report if this cannot be done at the place of the administrative offence and if the drawing up of a report is important, to ensure the correct and timely examination of administrative-offence cases, and to ensure the implementation of decisions in administrative-offence cases.

At the material time, Article 398.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO) of 2000 provided that administrative arrest, that is the short-term restriction of an individual's liberty, may be applied in exceptional circumstances when deemed necessary for ensuring the correct and timely examination of an administrative-offence case or for the implementation of a decision in an administrative-offence case, except for instances set out in legislation.

At the material time, Article 410.4 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO) of 2000 provided that a copy of the administrative-offence report shall be given to an individual who is subject to the administrative-offence proceedings or to a representative of a legal entity.

At the material time, Article 414.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO) of 2000 provided that a report concerning an administrative offence punishable by administrative detention shall be sent to a judge for examination immediately after it has been drawn up.

At the material time, Article 422.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO) of 2000 provided that cases concerning an administrative offence punishable by administrative detention shall be examined on the day of receipt by the court of an administrative-offence report, and cases against persons subjected to administrative arrest shall be examined at the latest within 48 hours of their arrest.
Under Article 368 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO) of 2000, a public prosecutor has a right to participate in administrative proceedings.
Chapter 28 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO) of 2000 enumerates the participants of administrative proceedings and their rights and obligations.

Chapter 28 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO) of 2000 does not mention the prosecution — a police officer, public prosecutor or any other public official representing the prosecution — as a participant of the proceedings.

Shortly after the demonstration had started, the police started to disperse it.
The applicant was arrested at around 6.10 p.m. on 19 June 2011 during the dispersal operation.
The applicant claimed that he had been arrested and taken to a police car by plain-clothed persons.
According to the official records, the applicant was arrested by police officers Z.H. and J.M.
The applicant was taken to police station No. 9 of the Sabail District Police Office.

Police officers Z.H. and J.M. submitted a report (raport) to a superior police officer stating that at around 6.10 p.m. they were on duty when Mammadov Gafgaz Suleyman oglu, whose identity was established later, was attempting to hold an unlawful demonstration.
Police officers Z.H. and J.M. stated in their report (raport) that they demanded that the applicant (Mammadov Gafgaz Suleyman oglu) stop his illegal actions.
Police officers Z.H. and J.M. stated in their report (raport) that the applicant deliberately disobeyed their demand and continued his actions.

Police officers Z.H. and J.M. stated in their report (raport) that for the reason of the applicant's deliberate disobedience they brought him to police station No. 9 of the Sabail District Police Office.
At 6.50 p.m. on 19 June 2011, an administrative-offence report (inzibati xəta haqqında protokol) was issued by police officer H.H. in respect of the applicant.

The administrative-offence report stated that by deliberately failing to comply with the lawful order of the police during the demonstration, the applicant had committed an administrative offence under Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO).
The applicant refused to sign the administrative-offence report.

The administrative-offence report contained a pre-printed text declaring that the arrested person was familiarised with the report, the reasons for his or her arrest, and his or her rights under Articles 371, 400.2, 401.1.6, and 401.1.7 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO) of the Republic of Azerbaijan were explained.
Subsequently, police officer H.H. prepared an administrative-arrest report (inzibati qaydada tutma haqqında protokol).
The administrative-arrest report prepared by police officer H.H. stated that the applicant was subjected to administrative arrest at 8 p.m. on 19 June 2011.

The administrative-arrest report stated that the applicant's administrative arrest was carried out in order to ensure issuance of an administrative-offence report, to ensure a correct and timely examination of the case, and to ensure the execution of decisions, in accordance with Articles 396.1.2 and 398 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO).
According to the applicant, he was never served with a copy of the administrative-offence report.
According to the applicant, he was never served with other documents in his case file.
According to the applicant, he was not given access to a lawyer after his arrest or while he was kept in police custody.
On 20 June 2011, the day after his arrest, the applicant was brought before the Sabail District Court.
According to the applicant, he refused the assistance of a State-funded lawyer and insisted on hiring a lawyer of his own choice.
According to the applicant, the judge disregarded his request to hire a lawyer of his own choice.
According to the applicant, his representation by the State-funded lawyer was ineffective and of a formalistic nature.
According to the applicant, the hearing before the Sabail District Court was very brief.
According to the applicant, members of the public, including human rights defenders and journalists, were not allowed to attend the hearing before the Sabail District Court.
The Sabail District Court had not taken a formal decision to close the hearing to the public.
The applicant stated before the Sabail District Court that he was not guilty of disobeying a lawful order of a police officer.
The applicant stated before the Sabail District Court that he had participated in the demonstration because he had a constitutional right to freedom of assembly.

According to the record of the hearing provided by the Government, the judge asked the applicant whether the police officers, before arresting him, had issued a relevant notice about dispersal of the demonstration.
According to the record of the hearing provided by the Government, the applicant answered that there were a lot of police officers and they were demanding that the demonstrators disperse.
According to the record of the hearing provided by the Government, the applicant stated that the police's demand to disperse was not lawful because the demonstrators were exercising their right.

According to the record of the hearing provided by the Government, the applicant stated that instead of calling on the demonstrators to disperse, the responsibility of the police should have been to ensure their security.
The only witness questioned during the court hearing before the Sabail District Court was police officer Z.H.

Police officer Z.H. testified that at around 6.10 p.m. on 19 June 2011 he noticed that the applicant, together with a group of other people, was attempting to hold an unauthorised demonstration by shouting out slogans.
Police officer Z.H. testified that he asked the applicant and the group of people to observe silence.
Police officer Z.H. testified that the applicant continued his actions, disobeying the police officers' requests.
According to the record of the hearing before the Sabail District Court, the State-funded lawyer stated that the applicant was not guilty.
According to the record of the hearing before the Sabail District Court, the State-funded lawyer asked the court to take into consideration the applicant's age and the fact that he had children.
The Sabail District Court found that the applicant had failed to stop participating in the unauthorised demonstration.
The Sabail District Court convicted the applicant under Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO).
The Sabail District Court sentenced the applicant to five days' administrative detention.
The applicant lodged an appeal before the Baku Court of Appeal arguing that his conviction was in violation of his rights because the demonstration in which he had participated had been peaceful.
The applicant complained before the Baku Court of Appeal that his arrest had been unlawful.
The applicant complained before the Baku Court of Appeal that the hearing before the Sabail District Court had not been fair.
The applicant urged the Baku Court of Appeal to quash the Sabail District Court's decision.
The applicant was represented before the Baku Court of Appeal by a lawyer of his own choice.
On 24 June 2011, the Baku Court of Appeal dismissed the applicant's appeal.
On 24 June 2011, the Baku Court of Appeal upheld the decision of the Sabail District Court, stating that its findings had been correct.
